title: My Money My Way: Taking Back Control of Your Financial Life
author: Kumiko Love
target_audience: Young adults and adults seeking to gain financial control
Individuals struggling with budgeting and debt
Beginner to intermediate personal finance readers
Anyone interested in mindset-based approaches to money
core_themes: Budgeting strategies tailored to individual values
Breaking free from financial shame and stress
primary_purpose: To empower readers to take control of their finances through practical tools, nonjudgmental advice, and mindset shifts, ultimately helping them create a financial system that aligns with their values and goals.

structure_format.narrative_style: Supportive, encouraging, personal story–driven with practical instruction
structure_format.organization: Divided into cohesive chapters that blend personal anecdotes, mindset exercises, and actionable steps
features: Real-life examples from the author and her community
Tips for overcoming overwhelm and comparison

key_concepts_lessons: There is no one-size-fits-all budget; personalization is key.
Mindset—the way we think and feel about money—influences financial behaviors.
Tracking expenses and knowing your numbers are foundational to change.
Budgeting can be a tool for self-care and personal empowerment, not restriction.
Financial shame and comparison with others are common but can be overcome.
Sustainable financial change comes from gradual, value-aligned steps.
notable_features: Focus on emotional and psychological barriers to money management
Blends worksheet-based tools with mindset coaching
Centered on inclusivity and relatability, drawing from diverse backgrounds
Leverages author’s own experience as a single mother to inspire readers
cultural_historical_context: Emerging during a period of increased financial insecurity (post-pandemic years), the book reflects growing awareness of the psychological impact of money and the need for accessible, personalized advice for people from various walks of life.
reception_impact: Praised for relatability and concrete, judgment-free guidance
Recognized in personal finance circles for its fresh, empowering take on budgeting
Helps fill a gap for those overwhelmed by traditional, rigid money advice
Popular among followers of The Budget Mom community
comparable_titles: You Need a Budget by Jesse Mecham
The Budgeting Workbook by Crystal Paine
The Financial Diet by Chelsea Fagan
Get Good with Money by Tiffany Aliche
